items.title: Added image glitch effect that uses quil's blend
items.body:
## What is it?

This glitch effect will take an image, split it into a series of n sized "pixel" squares then apply a blend effect. [Blend](http://quil.info/api/image/pixels#blend) can be given two separate pixels to perform a sort of differential (not sure if that really applies, my calc is over 7 years old). There are also a handfull of different "blend effects". I've picked out some of the best bellow.
### Blend

![blend](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/362269/12542273/d19fbb94-c2ee-11e5-98a3-38a390632841.gif)
This is my favorite effect and what I was originally trying to achieve. It takes two pixels from the image and swaps them.
### Difference

![difference](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/362269/12542326/d2c06cde-c2ef-11e5-9cb1-ea74dfd74d63.gif)
### Multiply -> Screen w/no differential

![mult_screen](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/362269/12542417/f5c5ca3e-c2f0-11e5-898b-6fa75e8de79e.gif)
### Multiply -> Screen w/differential

![mult_screen_d](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/362269/12542529/707056ea-c2f2-11e5-8865-56c82c650f48.gif)
### Soft Light -> Hard Light w/no differential

![soft_hard_nod](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/362269/12542484/b114cd12-c2f1-11e5-9cba-96f5614ae1a8.gif)
### Soft Light -> Hard Light w/differential

![hard_soft_d](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/362269/12542502/f4c3a240-c2f1-11e5-9fd3-da9bcd204817.gif)
### RANDOM

![random](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/362269/12542558/e13be952-c2f2-11e5-9307-c59caba782cd.gif)
100% random effect for each pixel changed

items.title: binding_of_caller warning
items.body:
The binding_of_caller warning is not appropriate. Some people use jruby and cannot install it or may just not want to have that gem installed. This makes the warning annoying. The lack of presence from this gem is not something you should be warning developers about. :relaxed: 

Great work! If this pull request is accepted then I would consider putting this into every one of my ruby projects as apart of the standard new template. 

Lets just remove this warning especially since some dev's cannot even install the gem because of their selected ruby.
